payload.title: 9 Engagement Ring Settings for an Active Lifestyle
payload.excerpt: Bezel, flush, low claw and more: 9 engagement ring settings rated for snag risk, stone protection and upkeep, plus ring care for sport and travel.
key_takeaways: A full bezel is the safest all-round choice for active hands, trading a little sparkle for a smooth, covered edge.
If you love claws, choose six over four, keep the head low and have them checked every six months.
Tension, channel and bar settings can be hard or even impossible to resize, so confirm the size before you order.
For diving, climbing, skiing and gym days, a plain or flush-set travel band keeps the engagement ring safe.

faq.q: Is it okay to wear an engagement ring while working out?
faq.a: It is safer to swap to a plain or flush-set band, as exercise and knocks take their toll.

faq.q: What is the most durable engagement ring setting?
faq.a: A full bezel or a flush setting. GIA calls bezels a practical choice for active hands and rates flush settings as hard wearing and unlikely to snag.

faq.q: What is the most common engagement ring setting, and is it good for active hands?
faq.a: Many classic engagement rings are claw solitaires, and they can work on active hands with care: raised claws can catch and need regular checks, so choose six claws and a low head.

faq.q: Is a bezel setting good for an active lifestyle?
faq.a: Yes: it resists chips and is less likely to catch on gloves, at the cost of slightly less light.

faq.q: Is platinum or gold better for an active lifestyle engagement ring?
faq.a: Platinum is very wear resistant; higher karat gold is softer and dents more easily.

faq.q: Should I take my engagement ring off to swim, surf or dive?
faq.a: Yes. Chlorine can loosen claws, so remove it before pools and hot tubs, and wear the travel band in the ocean.
